data.name: StiklingForQ
data.value: What is Stikling for?
data.comment: Question in the "Getting started" part of the Help page.

data.name: StiklingForA1
data.value: Keeping track of your houseplants and the new plants you grow from them, with a history of notes and photos for each one. It also keeps a care log, pest treatments, and the pots, soil mixes and fertilisers you use, but all of that is optional. A plant with just a name is fine.
data.comment: Answer to "What is Stikling for?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: PropagationQ
data.value: What is a propagation?
data.comment: Question in the "Getting started" part of the Help page.

data.name: PropagationA1
data.value: A new plant you are growing from one you already have, or from seeds. A cutting in a glass of water is the usual example. Others are a corm, an offset or pup, a leaf, a division, an air layer, and seeds. Stikling calls all of them propagations and keeps them apart from your plants until they have rooted and you pot them up.
data.comment: Answer to "What is a propagation?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: PropagationA2
data.value: Stikling is the Danish word for a cutting.
data.comment: Answer to "What is a propagation?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: WhereStartQ
data.value: Where do I start?
data.comment: Question in the "Getting started" part of the Help page.

data.name: WhereStartA1
data.value: Add a plant from Plants with the + button. A name is all it needs, and the rest can be filled in later. A plant's page opens on its photos and notes, with buttons for Photo, Note and Care. When you take a cutting from it, tap the three dots next to them, then Propagate.
data.comment: Answer to "Where do I start?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: WhereStartA2
data.value: Have plants already? Before you've added anything, the Today page also offers to add several at once, or to start a plant from old photos so its history goes back to when you got it.
data.comment: Answer to "Where do I start?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: TryBeforeAddingOwnPlantsQ
data.value: Can I try it before adding my own plants?
data.comment: Question in the "Getting started" part of the Help page.

data.name: TryBeforeAddingOwnPlantsA1
data.value: When nothing has been added yet, Today has a Show me around button. It loads an example coleus with a cutting in water and a young plant grown from an earlier cutting, with photos and notes, and shows you around the app with it in five short steps. Skip the tour and the example stays to look at. A row on Today removes it again, along with anything added to it. Plants made from it stay.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I try it before adding my own plants?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: SeeTourAgainQ
data.value: Can I see the tour again?
data.comment: Question in the "Getting started" part of the Help page.

data.name: SeeTourAgainA1
data.value: Yes, at any time: Settings, then Show me around. It loads the example again if you removed it, and asks at the end whether to keep it.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I see the tour again?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.value: How do I put it on my phone's home screen?
data.comment: Question in the "Getting started" part of the Help page.

data.name: PutOnPhoneSHomeA1
data.value: On an iPhone, open Stikling in Safari, tap the Share button, and pick Add to Home Screen.
data.comment: Answer to "How do I put it on my phone's home screen?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.comment: Answer to "How do I put it on my phone's home screen?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: PutOnPhoneSHomeA3
data.value: It then opens like any other app, without the browser around it. It is still the same app and the same data, so nothing has to be moved.

data.name: PutOnPhoneSHomeA4

data.comment: Answer to "How do I put it on my phone's home screen?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.comment: Question in the "Getting started" part of the Help page.

data.name: UseOnComputerA1

A plant or propagation page shows its details next to its history, and the buttons that sit at the bottom of the page on a phone are above the history instead. Today puts what needs doing in a wide column with the rest beside it, and Water plants shows the plants side by side. In the lists, the round + button is a button next to the title.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I use it on a computer?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: UseOnComputerA2Variant
data.value: Each device keeps its own plants until you sign in on both, which keeps them the same.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I use it on a computer?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are. Replaces {0} in the answer it belongs to.

data.name: UseOnComputerA2Variant2
data.value: Each device keeps its own plants. To move them, save a backup on one and restore it on the other.

data.name: SearchEverythingAtOnceQ
data.value: Can I search everything at once?
data.comment: Question in the "Getting started" part of the Help page.

data.name: SearchEverythingAtOnceA1
data.value: Tap the magnifier at the top, or Search in the menu on a computer, where the / key opens it too. It looks through your plants, cuttings, wishes, pots, mixes, feeds, products, rooms and tags, and the notes on every history, care log, problem and pest case. Tap a note to go to it. Notes are searched once every word you type has at least two letters. The search boxes on the Plants, Propagations and Wishlist pages still search just that list.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I search everything at once?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: SectionYourDataBackups
data.value: Your data and backups
data.comment: Heading of a section on the Help page.

data.name: WhereDataKeptQ
data.value: Where is my data kept?
data.comment: Question in the "Your data and backups" part of the Help page.

data.name: WhereDataKeptA1
data.value: On this device, in the browser's own storage. If you sign in, it is also kept on the Stikling server, photos included, so your other devices get it too. Without an account, nothing you add leaves this device unless you save a backup and move it yourself.
data.comment: Answer to "Where is my data kept?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: WhereDataKeptA2
data.value: On this device only, in the browser's own storage. There is no account and no server, so nothing you add leaves this device unless you save a backup and move it yourself.
data.comment: Answer to "Where is my data kept?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: AppSendAnythingWhenSomethingQ
data.value: Does the app send anything when something goes wrong?
data.comment: Question in the "Your data and backups" part of the Help page.

data.name: AppSendAnythingWhenSomethingA1
data.value: Yes. When something fails, the app sends a short error report to Sentry, so it can be fixed without anyone having to write in. It says what failed and where in the code. It never has your plants, notes or photos, and has no IP address or account. You can turn it off with Send error reports in Settings, and the privacy page says exactly what a report holds.
data.comment: Answer to "Does the app send anything when something goes wrong?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: HappensIfClearBrowserOrQ
data.value: What happens if I clear the browser or delete the app?
data.comment: Question in the "Your data and backups" part of the Help page.

data.name: HappensIfClearBrowserOrA1
data.value: Your plants, propagations and photos go with it. Clearing the site data for Stikling, or deleting the installed app, removes everything, and without a backup there is no way to get it back.
data.comment: Answer to "What happens if I clear the browser or delete the app?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: HappensIfClearBrowserOrA2
data.value: Some browsers also clear data by themselves when the phone runs low on space, or when a site hasn't been opened for a while. Installing Stikling to the home screen usually stops that. Under Backup and storage in Settings you can see whether the browser has agreed to keep your data, and ask it to.
data.comment: Answer to "What happens if I clear the browser or delete the app?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: BackUpQ
data.value: How do I back up?
data.comment: Question in the "Your data and backups" part of the Help page.

data.name: BackUpA1
data.value: Open Settings, then Backup and storage, and tap Save a backup. You get a ZIP file with everything in it, photos included. Keep it somewhere other than the phone, like cloud storage or your computer.
data.comment: Answer to "How do I back up?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: BackUpA2
data.value: If you're signed in, the backup fetches the full-size photos this device hasn't opened yet, so it can take a while the first time.
data.comment: Answer to "How do I back up?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: BackUpA3
data.value: Today reminds you when you haven't taken a backup, or when the last one is 30 days old.
data.comment: Answer to "How do I back up?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: GetPhotosOutAppQ
data.value: Can I get my photos out of the app?
data.comment: Question in the "Your data and backups" part of the Help page.

data.name: GetPhotosOutAppA1
data.value: Under Backup and storage in Settings, tap Download photos. You get a ZIP file with a folder for each plant, propagation and pot, and every photo is named by the date it was taken. Reference photos go in a Reference folder inside their plant's, or can be left out. The backup has the photos too, but it is made for Stikling to read back, so use this one to keep them or look through them on a computer.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I get my photos out of the app?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: GetPlantsIntoSpreadsheetQ
data.value: Can I get my plants into a spreadsheet?
data.comment: Question in the "Your data and backups" part of the Help page.

data.name: GetPlantsIntoSpreadsheetA1
data.value: Under Backup and storage in Settings, tap Plants as CSV or Propagations as CSV. You get a file that Excel and Google Sheets can open. It's a copy to read and sort, not a backup: importing the plants file again brings back the plants and their details, but not their photos, history or care.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I get my plants into a spreadsheet?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: MoveNewPhoneQ
data.value: How do I move to a new phone?
data.comment: Question in the "Your data and backups" part of the Help page.

data.name: MoveNewPhoneA1
data.value: The easiest way is to sign in on the new phone with the same account. Everything that has synced comes over by itself, photos included. A bar at the bottom shows while your things are being fetched, and photos can take a little longer to appear. Check that the old phone has finished syncing first, on the Account page in Settings.
data.comment: Answer to "How do I move to a new phone?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: MoveNewPhoneA2
data.value: Without an account, save a backup on the old phone, get the file over to the new one, open Stikling there and tap Restore a backup under Backup and storage in Settings.
data.comment: Answer to "How do I move to a new phone?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: MoveNewPhoneA3
data.value: Save a backup on the old phone, get the file over to the new one, open Stikling there and tap Restore a backup under Backup and storage in Settings.
data.comment: Answer to "How do I move to a new phone?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: MoveNewPhoneA4
data.value: A restore adds to what is already there instead of replacing it. Anything missing is added, anything deleted since the backup comes back, and where the same thing was changed in both places, the newer version wins, so a newer one in the backup replaces the one on the device. Restoring the same backup twice does no harm.
data.comment: Answer to "How do I move to a new phone?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: MoveNewPhoneA5
data.value: Before it restores, Stikling saves a backup of what is on the device now to your downloads, named stikling-before-restore with the date. If the restore removed something you wanted, restore that file to bring it back. It brings back what was deleted, but not edits the restore replaced with newer ones.
data.comment: Answer to "How do I move to a new phone?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: UseOnTwoDevicesQ
data.value: Can I use it on two devices?
data.comment: Question in the "Your data and backups" part of the Help page.

data.name: UseOnTwoDevicesA1
data.value: Yes. Sign in with the same account on both, and what you add or change on one shows up on the other, photos too.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I use it on two devices?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: UseOnTwoDevicesA2
data.value: Not at the same time. Each device has its own copy and they don't sync. You can move your data across with a backup and a restore whenever you switch.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I use it on two devices?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: NeedAccountQ
data.value: Do I need an account?
data.comment: Question in the "Your data and backups" part of the Help page.

data.name: NeedAccountA1
data.value: No. An account is optional, and everything in Stikling works without one. To make one, open Settings, then Sign in, and sign in with Google, Facebook or Discord, or with your email.
data.comment: Answer to "Do I need an account?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: NeedAccountA2
data.value: With an account, your plants are kept the same on every device you sign in on. If the phone already has plants on it when you sign in, they are added to what your account has, so nothing is lost.
data.comment: Answer to "Do I need an account?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: WhenSyncQ
data.value: When does it sync?
data.comment: Question in the "Your data and backups" part of the Help page.

data.name: WhenSyncA1
data.value: When you open the app, a couple of seconds after you change something, when the connection comes back, and every few minutes while the app is open. The Account page in Settings shows when it last synced, and has Sync now. If something goes wrong, a dot shows on the Settings gear.
data.comment: Answer to "When does it sync?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: WhenSyncA2
data.value: Photos go up from the device they were added on. Every device keeps a small copy of each photo, so lists look complete even offline, and fetches the full size when you open one. Once fetched, it stays on the device. With a lot of photos, the first sync on a new device takes a few minutes, and they fill in as they arrive.
data.comment: Answer to "When does it sync?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: WhenSyncA3
data.value: Without a connection, everything works as usual and your changes wait on the phone until they can be sent. If the same thing was changed on two devices, the newer change wins, the same as when a backup is restored.
data.comment: Answer to "When does it sync?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: ThereLimitOnPhotosQ
data.value: Is there a limit on photos?
data.comment: Question in the "Your data and backups" part of the Help page.

data.name: ThereLimitOnPhotosA1
data.value: Each account has 1 GB for photos on the server, which is roughly 2,500 photos. When it is nearly full, the Account page in Settings says how much is used. If it fills up, new photos stay on the device they were added on, and deleting photos you don't need makes room. The photos on your device aren't limited by this.
data.comment: Answer to "Is there a limit on photos?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: HappensWhenSignOutQ
data.value: What happens when I sign out?
data.comment: Question in the "Your data and backups" part of the Help page.

data.name: HappensWhenSignOutA1
data.value: You choose whether to keep a copy on this device or remove it. What has synced stays with your account either way and comes back when you sign in again.
data.comment: Answer to "What happens when I sign out?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: HappensWhenSignOutA2
data.value: Signing out sends your latest changes first, and tells you if any changes or photos haven't reached the server yet. Removing the data would delete those, so save a backup first if you want to keep them.
data.comment: Answer to "What happens when I sign out?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: SeeServerHasAboutMeQ
data.value: Can I see what the server has about me?
data.comment: Question in the "Your data and backups" part of the Help page.

data.name: SeeServerHasAboutMeA1
data.value: Yes. On the Account page in Settings, tap Download your data. You get a ZIP with everything the Stikling server holds about you: your plants and everything else you added, your photos, your settings, and what the sign-in service has, like your email address. The files inside are plain text and open in any text editor.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I see what the server has about me?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: SeeServerHasAboutMeA2
data.value: When you delete something, the server removes it and only keeps a note that it was deleted, so your other devices delete it too.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I see what the server has about me?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: DeleteAccountQ
data.value: How do I delete my account?
data.comment: Question in the "Your data and backups" part of the Help page.

data.name: DeleteAccountA1
data.value: On the Account page in Settings, tap Delete account at the bottom. It erases everything your account has on the Stikling server, photos included, and deletes your sign-in. It can't be undone.
data.comment: Answer to "How do I delete my account?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: DeleteAccountA2
data.value: You choose whether this device keeps what it has. If it does, the app carries on without an account, like before you signed in. Your other devices stop syncing and keep what is on them.
data.comment: Answer to "How do I delete my account?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: SectionPlants
data.value: Plants
data.comment: Heading of a section on the Help page.

data.name: AddLotPlantsAtOnceQ
data.value: Can I add a lot of plants at once?
data.comment: Question in the "Plants" part of the Help page.

data.name: AddLotPlantsAtOnceA1
data.value: Yes. On the add plant page, or on Today before you've added anything, tap Quick add or Add several at once, then type or paste a list of names, one per line or separated by commas. Names the app knows, botanical or everyday ones like snake plant, are filled in as genus, species and cultivar, and anything written after them goes into the notes. A name it doesn't know becomes the nickname, and so does an everyday name that two plants share, like money tree, so you can pick which one it is. Check the list, remove what you don't want, and tap the button to add them all.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I add a lot of plants at once?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: FindPlantLongListQ
data.value: How do I find a plant in a long list?
data.comment: Question in the "Plants" part of the Help page.

data.name: FindPlantLongListA1
data.value: Sort the list by genus or by room to get a heading for each group, with how many plants are in it. With 30 or more plants sorted A to Z or by genus, a column of letters down the right side jumps to a letter. You can also slide a finger along it. Search works too, and finds a plant by any of its names.
data.comment: Answer to "How do I find a plant in a long list?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: ManyPlantsHaveEachKindQ
data.value: How many plants do I have of each kind?
data.comment: Question in the "Plants" part of the Help page.

data.name: ManyPlantsHaveEachKindA1
data.value: Collection at the top of Plants shows how many plants, species and genera you have, the one you've had longest, and how many there are of each genus and in each room. Tap a genus or a room to see those plants.
data.comment: Answer to "How many plants do I have of each kind?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: KeepSeveralPlantsOnePotQ
data.value: Can I keep several plants in one pot?
data.comment: Question in the "Plants" part of the Help page.

data.name: KeepSeveralPlantsOnePotA1
data.value: Yes. Set how many are in the pot on the plant's edit page, for example five aloe pups kept as one plant. The number shows after its name in the lists.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I keep several plants in one pot?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: KeepSeveralPlantsOnePotA2
data.value: When some die, are given away or get a pot of their own, open the plant's three dots and tap Some of them. The ones you pot up on their own become plants of their own, with this one as their parent.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I keep several plants in one pot?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: KeepSeveralPlantsOnePotA3
data.value: When one plant goes into another plant's pot, tap Pot together on its page. It is then counted in the other plant and leaves the lists, but it keeps its history and can be opened from the other plant's page. Take it out again undoes it. Rooted cuttings can go straight into a plant's pot when you pot them up.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I keep several plants in one pot?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: WhyPotUpSayPotQ
data.value: Why does Pot up say the pot is much bigger?
data.comment: Question in the "Plants" part of the Help page.

data.name: WhyPotUpSayPotA1
data.value: A pot much wider than the last one keeps the soil wet for longer, which is a common cause of root rot. When you pick a new pot, the app shows the old and new width across the top, and says so when the new one is a lot wider. You can still use it, so water less until the roots fill it. Under Say when a new pot is much bigger in Settings you can change how much wider counts as a lot, 5 cm to start with. It needs the width set on both pots.
data.comment: Answer to "Why does Pot up say the pot is much bigger?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: BringPlantsFromSpreadsheetQ
data.value: Can I bring in my plants from a spreadsheet?
data.comment: Question in the "Plants" part of the Help page.

data.name: BringPlantsFromSpreadsheetA1
data.value: Yes. Save the sheet as CSV, or copy the cells with the headings, and open import a spreadsheet on the add plant page or under Backup and storage in Settings. Each of your columns is matched to a field, like the name, the room or the date you got it, and you can change any match. A column that matches no field becomes a field of its own, named after the heading, with the kind of field guessed from what is in it. You can switch it to a line in About it or leave it out, so nothing is lost, and dates for when a plant was last watered, fed or repotted go into its care log. Then check the plants: a row that looks like a plant you already have is left out unless you tick it. When it's done, Undo on the same screen removes everything the import added, the new fields too.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I bring in my plants from a spreadsheet?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: AddFieldAppDoesnTQ
data.value: Can I add a field the app doesn't have?
data.comment: Question in the "Plants" part of the Help page.

data.name: AddFieldAppDoesnTA1
data.value: Yes. Open Your fields in Settings, or tap Add a field of your own under More details on the plant form. A field can hold text, a number, a date or a choice from a list you set, like clone name, awards or humidity. It shows on the plant's page once you've filled it in, the search finds the text and the choices, and the spreadsheet export has a column for it. In the plant table each field can be a column and sorted by. A choice field, and How it was raised, can narrow the plant list with the Fields menu next to the filters. data.name: DormantQuarantineMeanA1

Quarantine is for a new or sick plant you are keeping apart from the rest. Both are started and ended with the three dots next to Photo and Note on the plant's page. They show as a badge, have a filter on the plant list, and are written on the plant's history when they start and end. A new plant can go straight into quarantine under More details when you add it. To have bought, swapped and gifted plants start there, turn on Quarantine new plants under Pests in Settings, and untick it on the form when a plant doesn't need it. A quarantine lasts 14 days unless you pick another length, and Quarantine length in Settings changes the one new quarantines start with. When it is up, the plant shows on Today so you can check it and let it out.

data.name: LogWateringFeedingQ
data.value: How do I log watering and feeding?
data.comment: Question in the "Plants" part of the Help page.

data.name: LogWateringFeedingA1
data.value: Open the plant and tap Care, next to Photo and Note. It shows when it was last watered, fed and so on, and logging is a tap. Under that, The last year is a calendar with a row for each month, showing the days it was watered, fed or had a meter reading, so gaps in the rhythm stand out. Tap a month to list the days in it. When it was last watered also shows under the plant's name, on the plant list and on the Water screen. A refill or top-up counts as water too, and a plant in a self-watering pot is logged as Refilled in Care. To log for several plants at once, tap Select on the plant list, pick them and tap Log care. The same bar can also add a note or tags to all of them, and Move puts them all in a room or spot. Plants already there are left alone. If you have a meter, tap Add EC and pH when logging a feed to note the readings, and they show on that line in the care history.
data.comment: Answer to "How do I log watering and feeding?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: LoggedCareWrongFixQ
data.value: I logged care wrong. How do I fix it?
data.comment: Question in the "Plants" part of the Help page.

data.name: LoggedCareWrongFixA1
data.value: Open the plant, tap Care and tap the entry under History. You can change the date, the meter reading, the water, EC and pH, or the note, and tap Save. Delete takes the entry out of the history and the watering reminder. What was done and its products can't be changed, so delete the entry and log it again. A line the entry added to the plant's history stays there until you delete it on its own. A cutting's care entries work the same way from its own care sheet, where you can remove them.
data.comment: Answer to "I logged care wrong. How do I fix it?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: WateringReminderWorkQ
data.value: How does the watering reminder work?
data.comment: Question in the "Plants" part of the Help page.

data.name: WateringReminderWorkA1
data.value: Turn it on under Watering reminder in Settings. It learns how often each plant gets water from what you have logged, and asks you to check the plant on Today when it is probably dry. It never tells you to water, and it never uses a care guide or a fixed number of days. It says nothing about a plant until it has seen a few waterings, so the first weeks are quiet. Until then the plant's page says how many more it needs. Log waterings as you do them and it gets better. It leans later when unsure, since a plant that is checked a day too late is better off than one watered too soon. When a plant watered from the top is due a check, Today has a How to tell if it needs water note under Water with a few ways to check.
data.comment: Answer to "How does the watering reminder work?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: WateringReminderWorkA2
data.value: If you log meter readings, it learns how long the plant takes to dry down to the level you water at, and that works as soon as one watering has been followed by a dry reading. This is for plants you water from the top. Semi-hydro (LECA and PON), corm risers, self-watering pots and plants with an outer pot you keep water in count how long the reservoir lasts instead, and the row says Refilled when you tick it. A plant in water is topped up, and the row says Topped up. When the way a plant gets water changes, like moving from soil to LECA, it starts learning again, since the old waterings say nothing about the new way. A gap across a trip or quiet time you have added under Away and quiet time isn't learned from either, unless a watering was logged during it.
data.comment: Answer to "How does the watering reminder work?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: WhyTodaySayEmptyOuterQ
data.value: Why does Today say to empty the outer pot?
data.comment: Question in the "Plants" part of the Help page.

data.name: WhyTodaySayEmptyOuterA1
data.value: A plant standing in an outer pot sits in the water that drains out after watering, and roots left in water for days can rot. An hour after you log a watering, Today asks you to tip it out, for plants with an outer pot where you don't keep water on purpose. Tap Emptied on the plant, or All emptied for the lot. Under Remind me to empty the outer pot in Settings you can change the wait or turn it off.
data.comment: Answer to "Why does Today say to empty the outer pot?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: KeepTrackPlantMovingLECAQ
data.value: How do I keep track of a plant moving to LECA or PON?
data.comment: Question in the "Plants" part of the Help page.

data.name: KeepTrackPlantMovingLECAA1
data.value: Change Grows in on its edit page and leave Track the move to semi-hydro ticked, or pick Moving to semi-hydro from the three dots on its page. Its page then has a checklist for washed roots, the first new water root and the first new leaf. Tap a step when it happens, and tap it again to take it off. Once a root and a leaf have both shown up, the page says it has settled in. If nothing new is ticked for 6 weeks, or the weeks you chose, Today asks you to have a look at its roots and leaves.
data.comment: Answer to "How do I keep track of a plant moving to LECA or PON?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: StillWetNoMeterOnQ
data.value: What do Still wet and No meter do on Today?
data.comment: Question in the "Plants" part of the Help page.

data.name: StillWetNoMeterOnA1
data.value: For a plant you water from the top, tap Still wet and pick what the meter reads, from 0 to 10. The reading is saved with the plant's care, and the plant comes back later, once it has had time to dry. No meter puts it off for a few days without a reading. For the other plants the button says Not yet and does the same. The tick logs the watering, refill or top up for today. The clock puts the row off for a day or more, like the other rows.
data.comment: Answer to "What do Still wet and No meter do on Today?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: WaterAtReadingQ
data.value: What is the Water at reading?
data.comment: Question in the "Plants" part of the Help page.

data.name: WaterAtReadingA1
data.value: It is the meter reading you water at, from 1 to 10, under Watering when you edit a plant that is watered from the top. It is 3 unless you change it, which is the top of the red dry part on most meters. Set it higher for a plant you keep moister, like a peace lily. To leave one plant out of the reminder, switch off Remind me to water there. It stays out of Today until you switch it back on.
data.comment: Answer to "What is the Water at reading?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: ReminderKnowAboutSeasonsGrowQ
data.value: Does the reminder know about the seasons and grow lights?
data.comment: Question in the "Plants" part of the Help page.

data.name: ReminderKnowAboutSeasonsGrowA1
data.value: Yes. Plants drink less as the days get shorter, so when the days are shortening the reminder leans later for a plant that has no light on it, and it uses the same weeks of earlier years when you have them. A plant under a grow light doesn't slow down in winter, so mark the room or spot as having one under Rooms and tags in Settings. Plants there are left out of the seasons. It also keeps the stretches a plant is dormant apart from the rest, so a plant's slow winter doesn't make the reminder late in spring.
data.comment: Answer to "Does the reminder know about the seasons and grow lights?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: TagsForQ
data.value: What are tags for?
data.comment: Question in the "Plants" part of the Help page.

data.name: TagsForA1

You can make a tag under Rooms and tags in Settings by picking the plants it goes on. There a tag can also be renamed, or merged into another one. Adding or removing a tag is written on the plant's history, so a tag like "flowering" still shows when it started and when you took it off.

data.name: SeePlantsAsPhotosOrQ
data.value: Can I see my plants as photos or as a table?
data.comment: Question in the "Plants" part of the Help page.

data.name: SeePlantsAsPhotosOrA1
data.value: Yes. The three buttons next to the sort switch between a list, a grid of photos and a table. The grid shows each plant's cover photo, with its name underneath. The table has a column for each detail, like a spreadsheet: when it was watered and fed, its room, what you paid and more. Tap a column's heading to sort by it, and tap it again to turn the order round. In the table, a Columns button takes the sort's place and picks which columns show. Drag them into your own order there, or use the arrows. Moisture is left empty once the plant has been watered since the reading, because the reading no longer says how the soil is. On a phone the table scrolls sideways with the name staying put. Each device remembers its own view, columns and sort.

data.value: What do the stages mean?
data.comment: Question in the "Propagations" part of the Help page.

data.name: StagesMeanA1

Moving it to Rooting there also notes today as the day of the first root, and the dates can be changed with Edit. For seeds the same stages are called Sown, Germinating and Sprouted.

data.name: StagesMeanA4

data.name: IfHaveSeveralCuttingsOneQ

data.name: TrackSeedsQ
data.value: Can I track seeds?
data.comment: Question in the "Propagations" part of the Help page.

data.name: PotUpQ
data.value: What does Pot up do?
data.comment: Question in the "Propagations" part of the Help page.

data.name: PotUpA1
data.value: It turns one or more from the propagation into plants in your collection. You find it, and Mark failed, behind the stage button on the propagation's page. Each new plant keeps a link to the plant the propagation came from, so you can always see where it started. It also takes the cutting's cover photo, and the plant's page shows the photos from when it was a cutting, marked As a cutting, with a link back to the propagation. They stay on the propagation. Both ask for a date, today unless you change it, so something you only found out a week later is recorded on the right day. When you mark one as failed you can also pick why (rotted, dried out, pests, mould, never rooted or don't know) and add a note. Both are optional, so it stays one tap.

data.name: PupAlreadyHasRootsPropagationQ

data.comment: Question in the "Propagations" part of the Help page.

data.name: PupAlreadyHasRootsPropagationA1

Start propagation links to this when the type is a pup or a division. data.name: LogWateringOnPropagationQ
data.value: Can I log watering on a propagation?
data.comment: Question in the "Propagations" part of the Help page.

data.name: LogWateringOnPropagationA1
data.value: Yes. Tap Care next to Photo and Note on its page. One in soil, bark, LECA or PON can be watered or given a moisture reading from 0 to 10, and one in water or on a corm riser gets Changed the water. The newest shows under its name, like "watered 2 days ago", and logging care counts as looking at it, so it stays off the list of propagations nobody has looked at. When it is potted up, its last watering goes with it to the new plant. A water change doesn't, since a plant in soil wasn't watered by it.

data.name: GiveAwayCuttingBeforeHasQ
data.value: Can I give away a cutting before it has rooted?

data.name: WaterLotPlantsAtOnceQ
data.value: How do I water a lot of plants at once?
data.comment: Question in the "Today" part of the Help page.

data.name: WaterLotPlantsAtOnceA1
data.value: Open Water plants from the top of the Plants list, or from the Water list on Today when plants are due. With several rooms, tap All rooms, or pick the rooms in the order you walk them and tap Start. The order is kept for next time. Pick Meter or Feel the soil at the top, then answer each plant: tap the meter's reading, from 0 to 10, or tap Dry or Still damp after pushing a finger into the soil. A plant that is dry shows a Watered button, and tapping it saves the watering at once. Undo on the row takes it back. A plant that is still damp only has a small Watered anyway. Nothing is ticked for you. A plant's feed comes with the button when it is due by that plant's setting, and change lets you pick another feed, or none. Plants in a reservoir or in water have a button to top up and nothing to read. You can also tap Watered on a plant you haven't checked. Feed this round at the top gives one feed with every watering there, unless a plant has its own feed due. Cuttings in soil or bark are listed under their room, after its plants, with the meter or Dry and Still damp too. A cutting has no feed, and Still damp on a cutting is only kept while the screen is open. Done shows what was watered.

data.name: WhyTodayAskIfPlantQ
data.value: Why does Today ask if a plant has gone dormant?
data.comment: Question in the "Today" part of the Help page.

data.name: WhyTodayAskIfPlantA1
data.value: When a plant's growing season is set under What it likes on its form, Today asks around the time its rest usually starts. That is from November for a plant that rests in winter (May in the southern hemisphere), and from June for one that rests in summer (December in the south). If it went dormant earlier than that, Today asks earlier the next year. Yes, it's dormant marks it dormant, and Not this year stops asking until next season. Plants without a season set are never asked, since most houseplants don't rest.
data.comment: Answer to "Why does Today ask if a plant has gone dormant?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

Notifications can also be blocked for Stikling in the browser or in the phone's settings, and a battery saver can hold them back until you pick the phone up. Send a test in Settings shows whether a notification reaches this device at all.

data.name: SharePlantOrCuttingA3
data.value: With two or more photos you can also make a before and after. Tap Share, then Before and after. It puts two photos side by side with the date on each and how long apart they were. It starts on the first and the newest photo, and you can change either one.
data.comment: Answer to "How do I share a plant or a cutting?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: SharePlantOrCuttingA4
data.value: With three or more photos you can make a time-lapse video. Tap Share, then Time-lapse. Each photo shows for a moment with its date and how long you had it, or the day count, in the order they were taken, and fades into the next. Choose Slow, Normal or Fast, and the size, and the preview plays on a loop. Tap a photo in the row to leave it out, and tap it again to put it back. At least two stay in, and a video takes up to 60 photos, so a longer history starts with 60 spread over it. Then tap Make video. It is made on your phone, without sound, so it takes a little while, and you can cancel it. When it is done, Share video opens the share menu and Save video keeps it as an MP4 you can post on TikTok or Reels. If you change anything after that, you make it again. Firefox on Android makes videos more slowly than other browsers.
data.comment: Answer to "How do I share a plant or a cutting?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: SharePlantOrCuttingA5
data.value: A plant's photos show how long you had it when they were taken, like 3 May 2026 · 1 yr 2 mo, counted from the date you got it. That needs the month you got it, and a full date to count the days in the first month. A propagation's photos show the day since it was started, like 3 May 2026 · day 24. Photos taken before that date get no count.
data.comment: Answer to "How do I share a plant or a cutting?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: ShareLinkPlantSPageQ
data.value: Can I share a link to a plant's page?
data.comment: Question in the "Photos and history" part of the Help page.

data.name: ShareLinkPlantSPageA1
data.value: Yes, if you're signed in. Tap Share on its page, then Link, then Make link. You get a link to a page anyone can open, without the app or an account, with its photos, milestones and notes from the first day to now. Post it with a cutting's progress, or send it to the friend who gave it to you. The page follows the plant, so new photos and notes show up on it after the next sync.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I share a link to a plant's page?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: ShareLinkPlantSPageA2
data.value: You choose what is on it. Switch off Show my notes to keep your notes to yourself, tap a photo to leave it out, and change the name and the line under it. The line starts as the one on the share card, like "Cutting from my Monstera", so change it if that says more than you want. The page never shows the room, the price, the shop or person it came from, who it went to, its tags, pots or care. While notes are shown, the note box on that plant says so.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I share a link to a plant's page?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: ShareLinkPlantSPageA3
data.value: Turn off the link stops the page within a few minutes, and so does deleting the plant, and anyone who opens the link sees that it is gone. Turning it on again makes a new link. A link needs an account because the page is shown from the Stikling server, using the photos your device has uploaded.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I share a link to a plant's page?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: ShareLinkPlantSPageA4
data.value: A plant that was potted up from a propagation shows the rooting it came from at the start of its page, up to the day it was potted up. After you mark a plant or a cutting as given away or sold, the app offers to send the link, so whoever got it can see its story and keep a copy in their own Stikling.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I share a link to a plant's page?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: SomeoneSentMeLinkTheirQ
data.value: Someone sent me a link to their plant. Can I keep its history?
data.comment: Question in the "Photos and history" part of the Help page.

data.name: SomeoneSentMeLinkTheirA1
data.value: Yes, once they have marked it as given away or sold. Open the link and tap Keep its history in Stikling. Stikling opens, shows what will be copied, and asks for a nickname, who gave it to you, its room, and for cuttings how many you got. The photos, milestones and the notes the page shows are copied to your device once, and kept under Before you got it on its page. They don't change if the page changes later, and they stay if the link is turned off. You don't need an account. If you delete it and open the link again, you can bring it back.
data.comment: Answer to "Someone sent me a link to their plant. Can I keep its history?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: BeforeYouGotQ
data.value: What is Before you got it?
data.comment: Question in the "Photos and history" part of the Help page.

data.name: BeforeYouGotA1
data.value: The history a plant or cutting had before it was given to you, copied from the link you were sent. It can't be edited, but you can frame its photos and pick one as the cover. Your own history starts at Arrived, above it. If you make a share link for it yourself, the page shows that history first, with its notes only while Show my notes is on, so it carries on to whoever you pass it to.
data.comment: Answer to "What is Before you got it?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: FixNoteWithWrongDateQ
data.value: How do I fix a note with the wrong date?
data.comment: Question in the "Photos and history" part of the Help page.

data.name: FixNoteWithWrongDateA1
data.value: Tap the pencil next to a note or photo in its history to change its text or date. The earlier version is kept and shown under edited. To write something down that happened earlier, tap Happened earlier? before adding the note or photo.
data.comment: Answer to "How do I fix a note with the wrong date?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: NoteComeBackNextYearQ
data.value: Can a note come back next year?
data.comment: Question in the "Photos and history" part of the Help page.

data.name: NoteComeBackNextYearA1
data.value: Yes. When you write a note, tap Bring it back and choose the same day next year or a day you pick. On that day the note shows on Today under Notes coming back. Tap Done when you have dealt with it, or Again next year to have it come back a year later. The pencil next to the note changes the day or takes it off.
data.comment: Answer to "Can a note come back next year?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: SpeakNoteInsteadTypingQ
data.value: Can I speak a note instead of typing it?
data.comment: Question in the "Photos and history" part of the Help page.

data.name: SpeakNoteInsteadTypingA1
data.value: Yes, with your keyboard's microphone key. On Android it is on the keyboard itself, or behind a long press on the comma or the space bar, and on an iPhone it is next to the space bar. It works in every field in the app, and the app never hears the recording.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I speak a note instead of typing it?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: SectionPestsProblems
data.value: Pests and problems
data.comment: Heading of a section on the Help page.

data.name: PestCaseQ
data.value: What is a pest case?
data.comment: Question in the "Pests and problems" part of the Help page.

data.name: PestCaseA1
data.value: One outbreak, like spider mites in the living room. A case covers the whole collection, one room, or the plants you pick, because pests spread and are treated together. You say how often to treat, and Today shows when the next round is due.
data.comment: Answer to "What is a pest case?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: WherePestsWhenHaveNothingQ
data.value: Where is Pests when I have nothing open?
data.comment: Question in the "Pests and problems" part of the Help page.

data.name: WherePestsWhenHaveNothingA1
data.value: Pests only gets a tab while a case is being treated or watched, or a plant has a problem that isn't over. The rest of the time the page, called Pests and problems, is under Supplies, with your old cases. To open a case for one plant, tap the three dots next to Photo and Note on its page, then Found pests.
data.comment: Answer to "Where is Pests when I have nothing open?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: SomethingSWrongWithPlantQ
data.value: Something's wrong with a plant. Where do I write it down?
data.comment: Question in the "Pests and problems" part of the Help page.

data.name: SomethingSWrongWithPlantA1
data.value: Open the plant, tap More, then Something's wrong. Pick what you see, like yellow leaves or root rot, and add a note or a photo. Later, tap How does it look? on the plant or the problem to say whether it's better, the same or worse and what you did. When it's over, say how it ended.
data.comment: Answer to "Something's wrong with a plant. Where do I write it down?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: SDifferenceBetweenProblemPestQ
data.value: What's the difference between a problem and a pest case?
data.comment: Question in the "Pests and problems" part of the Help page.

data.name: SDifferenceBetweenProblemPestA1
data.value: A pest case is for bugs, and can cover a whole room, with treatments on a schedule. A problem is for one plant and anything else that's wrong, like rot, sunburn or brown tips. It keeps what you tried and whether it helped.
data.comment: Answer to "What's the difference between a problem and a pest case?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: LookAgainQ
data.value: What does Look again do?
data.comment: Question in the "Pests and problems" part of the Help page.

data.name: LookAgainA1
data.value: When you log a problem or an update, you can ask to look again in a few days. On that day the plant shows on Today with How does it look? Pick No and nothing comes up.
data.comment: Answer to "What does Look again do?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: WillAppTellMeSQ
data.value: Will the app tell me what's wrong or what to do?
data.comment: Question in the "Pests and problems" part of the Help page.

data.name: WillAppTellMeSA1
data.value: No. It can't see the plant. When you log a problem, it shows what you did the last times one of your plants had the same, and how that ended, so you can decide.
data.comment: Answer to "Will the app tell me what's wrong or what to do?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: CheckPlantWithoutOpeningCaseQ
data.value: Can I check a plant without opening a case?
data.comment: Question in the "Pests and problems" part of the Help page.

data.name: CheckPlantWithoutOpeningCaseA1
data.value: Yes. Tap the three dots on the plant's page, then Check for pests. No signs logs that you looked it over, and the plant's page then shows when it was last checked. Found some opens a case instead. A check on a case counts too.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I check a plant without opening a case?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: AboutPlantsThatWereOutsideQ
data.value: What about plants that were outside for the summer?
data.comment: Question in the "Pests and problems" part of the Help page.

data.name: AboutPlantsThatWereOutsideA1
data.value: Mark the balcony or garden as outdoors under Rooms and tags in Settings. A spot in an outdoor room counts too. When you move a plant from there to an indoor room, Stikling offers to put it in quarantine and to log a check for pests. This works from the plant's edit page and when you move several plants at once from the Plants list. It only asks when a plant moves, never on a date.
data.comment: Answer to "What about plants that were outside for the summer?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: CheckNeighboursMeanQ
data.value: What does "Check the neighbours" mean?
data.comment: Question in the "Pests and problems" part of the Help page.

data.name: CheckNeighboursMeanA1
data.value: When a case is on plants you picked, the case lists the other plants in the same rooms, since pests spread to plants that stand close. Each shows when it was last checked. Clean logs a check on it, and Add to case puts it in the case.
data.comment: Answer to "What does "Check the neighbours" mean?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: DifferenceBetweenTreatingWatchingQ
data.value: What is the difference between treating and watching?
data.comment: Question in the "Pests and problems" part of the Help page.

data.name: DifferenceBetweenTreatingWatchingA1
data.value: While a case is Treating, each treatment you log moves the next one along by the interval (or the next step, if it follows a treatment plan), and the case shows when the next one is due once the first is logged. Until then, Today and the Pests and problems page show the case as having no treatment yet. Set it to Watching when the pests seem gone, and Today asks for a check once a week instead. If a check finds some, Found some puts it back to treating.
data.comment: Answer to "What is the difference between treating and watching?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: KnowWhenCaseOverQ
data.value: How do I know when a case is over?
data.comment: Question in the "Pests and problems" part of the Help page.

data.name: KnowWhenCaseOverA1
data.value: A case being watched counts the days since its last treatment, like Clean 12 of 28 days. It takes 4 weeks unless you change it under Pests in Settings. When the count is reached and you have logged a check in the last week, the case says it is ready to resolve, and Today lists it under Ready to resolve. It never resolves by itself, so tap Resolve when you agree. Finding pests again starts the count over.
data.comment: Answer to "How do I know when a case is over?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: StickyTrapCountsQ
data.value: What are sticky trap counts?
data.comment: Question in the "Pests and problems" part of the Help page.

data.name: StickyTrapCountsA1
data.value: Count what is on a yellow or blue sticky trap now and then, and the app works out how many were caught since last time. The chart of the catch per week shows whether the treatment is working. Thrips, fungus gnats and whitefly fly into traps, so their cases show the trap straight away. Other pests rarely end up on one, but if you have a trap up anyway, tap Count a sticky trap on the case.
data.comment: Answer to "What are sticky trap counts?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: SectionPotsMixesFertilisers
data.value: Pots, mixes and fertilisers
data.comment: Heading of a section on the Help page.

data.name: HaveFillPotsSoilMixesQ
data.value: Do I have to fill in pots, soil mixes and products?
data.comment: Question in the "Pots, mixes and fertilisers" part of the Help page.

data.name: HaveFillPotsSoilMixesA1
data.value: No. They are all under Supplies for anyone who wants them. Once they are there, a plant can pick its pot and mix from a list, and logging a feed says what went in the water without typing. A propagation that grows in soil can pick a mix too, and it goes on to the plants when you pot up.
data.comment: Answer to "Do I have to fill in pots, soil mixes and products?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: WithSoilMixQ
data.value: What can I do with a soil mix?
data.comment: Question in the "Pots, mixes and fertilisers" part of the Help page.

data.name: WithSoilMixA1
data.value: Save it under a name with what is in it. On the Soil mixes page, tap the number of plants next to a mix to see which plants are in it, and tap a plant to open it. If every ingredient has an amount, tap Measure out, type how much mix you want, and the app says how much of each ingredient to use.
data.comment: Answer to "What can I do with a soil mix?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: DifferenceBetweenProductFeedQ
data.value: What is the difference between a product and a feed?
data.comment: Question in the "Pots, mixes and fertilisers" part of the Help page.

data.name: DifferenceBetweenProductFeedA1
data.value: A product is one bottle or bag, like a fertiliser or silica, with the dose you usually use. A feed is several products mixed into the water together, in the order they go in. Fill in how much water you are mixing, and the app says how much of each to add. Tap the line saying how many plants a feed has been given to, and it lists the plants and the days they got it.
data.comment: Answer to "What is the difference between a product and a feed?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: NoteProductQ
data.value: Can I note what is in a product?
data.comment: Question in the "Pots, mixes and fertilisers" part of the Help page.

data.name: NoteProductA1
data.value: Yes. When you add or edit a product, you can fill in what it contains as printed on the label: N, P and K for a fertiliser, and other nutrients like calcium, magnesium or silicon for any product, under Add a nutrient. Type the numbers as the label gives them, in percent. Labels usually give phosphorus and potassium as oxides, and the app doesn't convert them. What you fill in shows under the product in the list, and next to its name when you pick products for a feed, so bottles that look alike are easy to tell apart.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I note what is in a product?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: FeedGoWithEveryWateringQ
data.value: Can a feed go with every watering?
data.comment: Question in the "Pots, mixes and fertilisers" part of the Help page.

data.name: FeedGoWithEveryWateringA1
data.value: Yes. Open the plant, tap Edit and look under Watering for Feed with the watering. Pick a saved feed, then choose every watering, every second watering or every third. After that, ticking Watered or Topped up logs the feed and its doses too, on the days it is due. It is off until you set it, and a plant with no saved feed to pick has to wait until you have saved one under Feeds.
data.comment: Answer to "Can a feed go with every watering?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: NurseryPotsOuterPotsQ
data.value: What are nursery pots and outer pots?
data.comment: Question in the "Pots, mixes and fertilisers" part of the Help page.

data.name: NurseryPotsOuterPotsA1
data.value: A nursery pot is the plain one the plant actually sits in, and an outer pot is the decorative one without drainage that it goes inside. Some pots are neither and stand on their own. The Pots page lists one kind at a time, and shows which of yours are in use and which are free. Containers for propagating, like a box with a lid, have their own tab. Picking a self-watering pot for a plant sets "Grows in" to LECA, and you can change it after.
data.comment: Answer to "What are nursery pots and outer pots?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: TellSimilarPotsApartQ
data.value: How do I tell similar pots apart?
data.comment: Question in the "Pots, mixes and fertilisers" part of the Help page.

data.name: TellSimilarPotsApartA1
data.value: Give each one a photo. Tap Photo beside a pot on the Pots page, or add photos while adding or editing it. The photo then shows beside the pot there, on the chips when you pick a pot for a plant, and on the page of each plant that uses it, where tapping it shows the pot's photos. The photos belong to the pot, not to a plant, so they stay with it when it moves to another plant. Open a pot's photos on the Pots page to choose which one is shown, frame it or delete one. Deleting a pot deletes its photos too.
data.comment: Answer to "How do I tell similar pots apart?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: TreatmentRecipesQ
data.value: What are treatment recipes?
data.comment: Question in the "Pots, mixes and fertilisers" part of the Help page.

data.name: TreatmentRecipesA1
data.value: Sprays and drenches you make up yourself against pests, like an alcohol spray. Save one under Supplies, and logging a treatment is then a tap. Mix a batch works out the amounts for any size of bottle.
data.comment: Answer to "What are treatment recipes?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: FollowSetTreatmentsLikeSprayingQ
data.value: Can I follow a set of treatments, like spraying twice and then predatory mites?
data.comment: Question in the "Pots, mixes and fertilisers" part of the Help page.

data.name: FollowSetTreatmentsLikeSprayingA1
data.value: Yes, with a treatment plan. Under Supplies, then Treatment plans, add the steps in order. Each step after the first says how many days after the step before it comes, and what it uses: one of your treatment recipes, or whatever you type. To use one, open a case and tap Follow a plan, or pick the plan when you open the case. The first step is due on the day you start.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I follow a set of treatments, like spraying twice and then predatory mites?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: FollowSetTreatmentsLikeSprayingA2
data.value: While the plan runs, Today and the case show the step that is up next. Log it when it's done, Skip it if you won't do it, or Move it to a later day. The next step counts from the day the one before was done or skipped, so a late spray moves the rest along. A treatment you log outside the plan, like an extra spray, doesn't move it on. After the last step Today asks whether to start watching the case or keep treating. If you keep treating, the case goes on at its interval. You can also stop a plan from the case at any time.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I follow a set of treatments, like spraying twice and then predatory mites?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.

data.name: FollowSetTreatmentsLikeSprayingA3
data.value: The case keeps its own copy of the steps, so changing or deleting the plan later doesn't change one that is running. A case without a plan works as before, with a treatment every few days at the interval you set.
data.comment: Answer to "Can I follow a set of treatments, like spraying twice and then predatory mites?" on the Help page. Keep the HTML tags where they are.
